title: Awards but no job, and the festival circuit
summary: Willard recalls an early-1960s moment of awards with no work; today festivals in America and Europe keep him busy.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I remember one particular time that I thought you received several awards in a period of about two months as being one of the most outstanding trumpet players who ever lived and, at that same particular time, you did not have a job.
WELL, that's about the size of it.
I thought that was quite ironic.
Yeah well, that has all ironed itself out really in later years.

And, the thing that has saved the jazz in this country - of course - are the many, many festivals each year and most of the jazz guys of my caliber depend on those things each year and I get them each year. But, now, I have added Europe to my playing now and I have as many festivals in Europe as I have in America - so, if I do them all---
I'm busy as hell and - at least - making some money doing what I do.
